description: Block known vulnerability scanners by User-Agent. Word-bounded and deduplicated: the old list matched 'zap' as a substring (blocking Zapier webhooks) and repeated nessus/openvas/qualys/netsparker.

Log header values carrying an encoded CRLF pair (%0d%0a / %0a%0d), a response-splitting probe if the backend decodes them. Raw \r/\n branches were removed (Go's server rejects them before the WAF runs) and a lone %0a no longer matches (it appears in legitimately encoded URLs inside Referer). Score 4 keeps it below the default threshold on its own.
Block SQL injection, XSS, and path traversal attempts in headers. Improved pattern matching.

Log requests referencing an opaque object id (UUID, or a 32/40-hex path segment) as a weak IDOR signal for correlation. Low score and does not block on its own -- IDOR cannot be decided from the request alone, so matching on common param names (id=, user=, file=) was removed to stop false positives.

Block Java serialized objects: the base64 form (rO0AB, case-sensitive: base64 is) and the hex form in either case. The old raw-bytes branch (\xac\xed...) was removed: Go's regexp engine compiles \xac as the rune U+00AC, which can never equal the raw 0xAC byte, so it had never matched.

Block path traversal attempts and direct access to sensitive files (Target: URI and Headers). Case-insensitive (percent-encoding is emitted in both cases on the wire) and includes a '..%252F' branch for traversal whose slashes are double-encoded.

Block high-confidence path traversal / LFI in the request body (form fields, JSON): '../' repeated (>=2) or direct access to a sensitive file. Conservative on purpose -- a single '../' does not fire -- to avoid false positives on legitimate relative paths in bodies. Complements path-traversal, which covers URI and HEADERS.

Block command injection in query arguments: a command following an injection metacharacter (; | ` $() or a raw %0a/%0d encoded newline), a read of a sensitive path, curl/wget fetching a URL, an interpreter with flags, or a pipe to a shell. Command list includes rm/nc/env/awk/sed/dd/chmod/mkfifo. '&' is still excluded (query-string separator).

Block access to sensitive dotfiles and server internals (.git, .env, .htaccess/.htpasswd, .svn, WEB-INF/META-INF, .dockerenv, server-status). The former generic branch (config|database|backup|...).(json|yaml|...) was removed: it blocked /config.json and similar files that frontends legitimately fetch.

Block SQL injection in query arguments: keyword pairs may have content between them but not a '&' (so ?select=name&from=2024 with two benign param names cannot pair up), plus quote-context tautologies (numeric and string operands), timing functions, and T-SQL/file primitives. BODY is covered by the stricter sql-injection-body rule so prose like 'select an item from the list' is not blocked.

Block SQL injection in the request body using high-confidence signals only: adjacent UNION [ALL|DISTINCT] SELECT, quote-context tautologies ('a'='a, 1=1, OR true), timing functions with a numeric argument, waitfor delay, xp_cmdshell, load_file, INTO OUTFILE, information_schema. Keyword pairs like select...from are deliberately NOT matched in bodies: they block English prose while real injections are caught by the signals above.

Block SSRF: URLs whose host is loopback/private/link-local, a bracketed IPv6 loopback/mapped/link-local address, a hex (0x7f...) or bare decimal IP, an .internal/.local/.intranet/.test name, or a cloud metadata endpoint. HEADERS was dropped as a target: the joined header string contains the Referer, and LAN referers (http://nas.local/) blocked every request from intranet apps.

Block SSRF to unspecified (0.0.0.0), link-local/metadata (169.254.*), and multicast (224-239.*) addresses. Class E / broadcast (240-255.*) was removed: it is unroutable, and matching it blocked every netmask parameter (255.255.255.0).

Block XSS: script tags, any on* event handler inside a tag (generic <tag ... on*= with whitespace OR slash separator, covering <svg/onload= and uncommon handlers like ontoggle/onpointerdown), iframe srcdoc, javascript:/vbscript: schemes, JS dialog/eval calls (no space before the paren, so prose like 'please confirm (by clicking)' and words ending in eval like 'retrieval(' do not match), and document.cookie/location.

Block double-percent-encoded injection metacharacters: %2527 ('), %2522 ("), %253C (<), %253E (>), %2500 (NUL). A legitimate client never needs to double-encode a quote, angle bracket, or null byte -- these survive one decode as %XX and target backends that decode twice. Deliberately excludes %252F (double-encoded slash), which appears in legitimate nested/re-encoded URL parameters; traversal with double-encoded slashes is handled by the path-traversal rule's '..%252F' branch instead.

Block Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) and similar JNDI lookup injection: ${...jndi...}, a jndi: scheme, or a nested ${...${...  lookup (the standard obfuscation, e.g. ${${lower:j}ndi:...}). Nested-brace CI template syntax like GitHub's ${{ ... }} does not match: the inner brace run contains no second '${'.

Block MongoDB operator injection in the shape it is actually delivered: a quoted "$op": JSON key or a [$op]= form-style parameter. Replaces the removed nosql-injection-attacks rule, which matched bare words (count, find, update, db) in any body.
